Let me analyze this conflict.

Register: "Mettler-Toledo (Changzhou) Precision Instruments Ltd."
Document: "Mettler-Toledo (ChangZhou) Scale & System Ltd."

These are both Mettler-Toledo entities in Changzhou, but they're actually different legal entities. Mettler-Toledo (Changzhou) Precision Instruments Ltd. and Mettler-Toledo (ChangZhou) Scale & System Ltd. — these are genuinely different subsidiary names. The "Scale & System" vs "Precision Instruments" is a substantive difference in the company name, not just spelling drift or legal-suffix drift.

Actually, let me think. Mettler-Toledo has multiple entities in Changzhou. There's "Mettler-Toledo (Changzhou) Precision Instruments Ltd." and "Mettler-Toledo (Changzhou) Scale & System Ltd." — these could plausibly be two different legal entities under the same corporate group. The difference isn't just case ("Changzhou" vs "ChangZhou" would be trivial), but the core name differs: "Precision Instruments" vs "Scale & System". That's a genuinely different company name.

The rules say: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

The certificate document is the legal instrument, so if the document says "Mettler-Toledo (ChangZhou) Scale & System Ltd." and the register says "Mettler-Toledo (Changzhou) Precision Instruments Ltd.", the fused record should carry the document's value since the certificate is the legal instrument naming the applicant.

However, one could argue that both belong to the same corporate family... but the rule is about entity identity, not corporate family. "Precision Instruments Ltd." vs "Scale & System Ltd." are different legal entities (indeed, Mettler-Toledo Changzhou has had multiple registered entities over time).

So verdict: different-entity, best_value = document's "Mettler-Toledo (ChangZhou) Scale & System Ltd."

Should I normalize the casing "ChangZhou" to "Changzhou"? The rules say spelling drift = same-entity, but here it's different-entity. The best_value = the document's. I'd keep the document's value as-is, perhaps. Or could normalize casing. The instruction says best_value = the document's. I'll use the document's string verbatim. Maybe keep it verbatim to be safe.
